title_tag: 7 Best Spa and Thermal Hotels in Budapest (2026)
meta_description: Budapest spa hotels compared: thermal pools on Margaret Island, rooftop pools, spa suites. Price per night, pools listed, guest scores and the walk to town.
h1: 7 Best Spa and Thermal Hotels in Budapest (2026)
h1_main: 7 Best Spa and Thermal Hotels in Budapest
author_role: 7 spa hotels compared on the pools and spa you get, price per night, guest scores and distance from the centre
lead: The right spa hotel in Budapest is the one that fits your stay: thermal water in the building, free for guests (that is Ensana Thermal on Margaret Island, the #1 pick, €111), a spa suite in the centre so the sights are walkable, a rooftop pool for summer, or a big pool with river views. If you only want a day of bathing, the thermal baths are compared separately. This page gets you to the right hotel in under a minute.

To make the choice easy, I compared all 7 on what decides a spa stay: which pools and saunas are listed (thermal or not, indoor or rooftop), the price for the same night, guest scores, and how far you are from downtown, checked on each hotel's own listing. Filter by thermal water, central location, river setting or price below, or scroll straight to the ranking.

guide.h2: Budapest Spa Hotels Side by Side
guide.html:
Prices are for the same night (Wednesday 10 March 2027, 2 adults, 1 room). Scores are out of 10; distance is from downtown.

What the numbers say: only the two Ensana hotels on Margaret Island give you thermal water in the building, and both cost less than the central spa hotels (€104–111). The trade-off is distance: 2.4–2.5 miles from downtown. If you want to walk to the sights and soak in the evening, Queen's Court (€120) and Continental (€97) are 0.5–0.6 miles from downtown with a pool each.

• Real thermal water, all day: #1 Ensana Thermal.
  • The best-rated spa stay: #2 Kozmo (9.5).
  • A suite with a kitchenette and a pool, central: #3 Queen's Court.
  • Laps with a river view: #4 Helia.
  • A rooftop pool in summer: #6 Continental.
  • A historic building on the island: #7 Ensana Grand.

Want 5-star service on top? See the luxury hotels, most of which have a pool too.

guide.h2: Before You Book: Spa Rules, Seasons and Bath Days
guide.html:
Kids and pools: Corinthia lets guests under 16 use the pool and spa tub only from 9 am to 3 pm, with an adult.

Seasonal pools: the outdoor pools at Ensana Thermal and on Continental's rooftop are summer-only. The indoor pools run all year.

Treatments cost extra: the medical and spa treatments at the Ensana hotels and Helia are paid on top of the room.

Add a public bath: staying central? A day at Széchenyi or Rudas fits easily; on a Saturday, Sparty is the night-time version.

faqs.q: Which Budapest hotels have thermal water?
faqs.a: Ensana Thermal Margaret Island has thermal pools free for guests, and Ensana Grand Margaret Island next door connects to the same spa through a heated underground hall.

faqs.q: What is the best spa hotel in central Budapest?
faqs.a: Kozmo Hotel Suites & Spa has the highest guest score here (9.5), with an indoor pool, sauna and hot tub, 1 mile from downtown. Queen's Court is the cheaper central option with a pool and kitchenette suites.

faqs.q: Which hotel in Budapest has a rooftop pool?
faqs.a: Continental Hotel Budapest lists a rooftop pool, open in the summer months, plus an indoor pool.

faqs.q: How much is a spa hotel in Budapest per night?
faqs.a: From €97 (Continental) to €163 (Kozmo) for 2 adults on a March weeknight. The two thermal hotels on Margaret Island cost €104–111.

faqs.q: Is the spa free for hotel guests?
faqs.a: At Ensana Thermal and Ensana Grand the spa area is free for guests; treatments cost extra. Check the other hotels' rate details for spa access.

faqs.q: How far is Margaret Island from the city centre?
faqs.a: The Ensana hotels are 2.4–2.5 miles from downtown, on the quiet northern half of the island.

methodology: We compared Budapest hotels listing a spa and pool on what decides a spa stay: which pools, saunas and thermal facilities are listed, the price for the same night (10 March 2027, 2 adults), the guest score and its sub-scores, distance from downtown and the rules around the pools, all from each hotel's live listing.

review: Ensana Thermal is the only hotel here with thermal water in the building, free for guests: a thermal pool, a recreational pool, a 56 ft swimming pool, a seasonal outdoor pool, several saunas and a steam room.
